# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_88/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_88/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform the join on 'city' as specified
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select only the target columns: ['city', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# Ensure correct types: city (string), fare (float), ride_id (int)
result = joined[['city', 'fare', 'ride_id']].copy()

# Convert types explicitly
result['city'] = result['city'].astype(str)
result['fare'] = result['fare'].astype(float)
result['ride_id'] = result['ride_id'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path without the index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_88/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_88/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_88/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (primary key), aggregate fare and ride_id by mean to match target schema and reduce duplicates
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean"
})

# ride_id should be integer type as per target schema
result["ride_id"] = result["ride_id"].round().astype(int)

# Write output to the specified file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_88/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
